trust_decision.summary: APEv2Parser.parseTags trusts the file-declared tag item size (tagItemHeader.size) and allocates that many bytes, with no check against the tag's remaining bytes, the file size, or the bytes a stream actually delivers.

landing_point.why: The summary names the APEv2 parser plus memory allocation; the only explicit `new Uint8Array(tagItemHeader.size)` in parseTags is the binary/cover-art branch.

fix_sites.entry_point: parseBuffer/parseStream/parseFile/parseBlob/parseWebStream on APE, WavPack, Musepack, or MP3/ID3v1-trailing files (tag item size bookkeeping + key peek)
same public parse* APIs; utf-8 text item value
same public parse* APIs with skipCovers=false; binary/cover item value

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All published changes are in lib/apev2/APEv2Parser.ts parseTags (fix.diff:5-88). parseTags is also reached from lib/id3v1/ID3v1Parser.ts:140-143 (APE footer found by lib/core.ts:116-126 at the end of MP3/other files), but the fix covers that caller without touching it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 route at lib/apev2/APEv2Parser.ts:113-115: it is the footer-only fallback, not tag item parsing, and its size comes from the caller-supplied fileInfo.size (parseStream/parseWebStream argument), not from the file's declared item size, so it is the caller's fault.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Large legitimate values must still parse: multi-chunk (>64 KiB) text and cover values on non-random-access streams, the item after them, and NUL-separated multi-value text. A fixed size cap or a rejection of every stream without a known size would break these. The fix diff's own tests check this.

O6_input_shapes: external_info / reserved items (types 2,3), which only call ignore(), still get the size-vs-tag/file bound
item size larger than the remaining tag bytes but within the file
item size beyond the file (random-access tokenizer with known size)
stream tokenizer with an inflated caller-supplied fileInfo.size
key without a NUL terminator inside the tag boundary

O8_uncovered_routes.route: tryParseApeHeader fallback allocates a buffer of fileInfo.size - position before any bytes are read; on a stream with an inflated or untrusted advertised size, this is an unbounded allocation the fix did not touch.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Footer-only fallback, not tag item parsing; the size comes from caller-provided fileInfo rather than the file's declared item size.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 40 lines above the fix sites

O8b_injection_room.sibling: findApeFooterOffset could read the full APE tag body (offset - tagFooter.size) into one buffer sized from the footer's declared size, for a pre-scan.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already reads the footer and computes offset -= tagFooter.size with no bound; reading the whole tag in one go is the obvious optimisation for the random-access path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The ID3v1 trailing-APE path could pre-read footer.size bytes into a buffer and parse it via fromBuffer, the same way parseTagFooter does at lib/apev2/APEv2Parser.ts:85-91.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This copies an existing in-file pattern (buffer-then-fromBuffer) in another package, which also gives the distance that helped in the lessons.

O9_family: CWE-789 uncontrolled memory allocation from an untrusted length field (resource exhaustion)

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=18, yarn, tsc (typescript ^6), mocha; deps strtok3 ^10.3.5, token-types ^6.1.2
O10_build.project_tests: test/test-file-ape.ts, test/test-file-wavpack.ts, test/test-file-musepack.ts, test/test-file-mp3.ts (APE sample files); the fix adds test/test-apev2-lengths.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (tagItemHeader.size > bytesRemaining) throw` only before the cover-art allocation at lib/apev2/APEv2Parser.ts:171, leaving the text route (line 160), the stream case with unknown/inflated size, and the fallback buffer (line 114) open.

out_of_scope_notes: Recent pinned-tree commits fix the same allocation class in EBML and MP4 stsd (separate advisories); other tag parsers may have similar length-trusting allocations, not pursued.
